entries.objective: To clarify the technical mechanism of the Sporadic Server, especially budget consumption, replenishment, assumptions, and overhead.
entries.prompt: Based on my topic assigned from Prof. “Sporadic Server”. Explain the algorithm at a technical but beginner-friendly level. Focus only on the main mechanism: server budget, replenishment period, how aperiodic jobs are served, why the server protects periodic hard real-time tasks, and what overhead or implementation complexity it introduces. Do not write final seminar text; give me points that I can verify and rewrite in my own words.
entries.ai_output_summary: The LLM explained that a Sporadic Server reserves a limited execution capacity for aperiodic jobs. The server can execute irregular requests only while budget is available. When budget is consumed, the consumed amount is replenished later instead of being restored immediately. This makes the server responsive to aperiodic events while limiting processor interference against periodic hard real-time tasks. The AI also identified implementation overheads such as budget tracking, replenishment queue management, timer handling, and possible additional context switches.

actions: I compared the explanation with the original Sporadic Server paper by Sprunt, Sha, and Lehoczky and with accessible lecture notes on resource reservation servers. I checked whether the main mechanism was correctly described: limited server capacity, delayed replenishment, aperiodic job execution, and protection of periodic tasks. I also checked whether the mentioned overheads are reasonable from an implementation point of view.

issues: The explanation was useful for understanding the concept, but it did not provide a complete formal replenishment rule or full schedulability proof. These parts still need to be checked carefully from academic references before being included in the final paper.

entries.objective: To understand how Sporadic Server differs from Polling Server and Deferrable Server, so that I can explain the motivation and technical contribution more clearly in Milestone 1.
entries.prompt: As you know I'm working on “Sporadic Server”. I currently do not have access to Buttazzo’s book, so I am using accessible academic sources for initial understanding. Please explain the difference between Polling Server, Deferrable Server, and Sporadic Server at a beginner-friendly technical level. Focus on why Sporadic Server was introduced, what problem it solves better than the other two, and what assumptions or limitations I should mention. Do not write final seminar text; give me points that I can verify and rewrite in my own words.
entries.ai_output_summary: AI explained that Polling Server, Deferrable Server, and Sporadic Server are all mechanisms for serving aperiodic tasks in real-time systems. Polling Server checks for aperiodic work periodically and may waste capacity if no request is available. Deferrable Server keeps its capacity during a period, which improves response time but may create more interference with periodic tasks. Sporadic Server also preserves responsiveness, but uses delayed replenishment of consumed capacity to better control processor demand. The AI suggested using this comparison to explain why Sporadic Server is technically relevant.

actions: I checked the comparison against accessible real-time systems lecture material and the original Sporadic Server paper. I focused on whether the explanation correctly describes the motivation for Sporadic Server: improving aperiodic response time while limiting interference with hard real-time periodic tasks. I also checked that I do not present the comparison as copied textbook text.

issues: The comparison was useful for understanding the motivation, but it was still a simplified explanation. I need to verify exact technical details, especially replenishment behavior and schedulability conditions, before using them in the final paper.
